Near the far archway, a single flagstone sits a thumb’s width lower than the rest, its edge faintly scuffed by the grind of hidden machinery beneath.

Do you try to disable the tripwire, or skirt around both triggers and move on?

You keep your voice low and your words sparse, suggesting you belong to the next shift and that the warden has already signed the ledger. The guard, a hollow-eyed man in rust-scabbed mail, studies the shadows behind you more than he studies your face. After a moment that stretches too long, he grunts and steps aside, jerking his chin toward the black maw of the corridor beyond. He does not ask for proof. The way is open.
